data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Miscellaneous systemic drugs_

**Class:** Non-steroidal pure anti-androgen (androgen receptor antagonist)

## Mechanism of action
- Competitively blocks androgen receptors in target tissues (hair follicle, sebaceous gland, prostate)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Prostate cancer (approved)
- Off-label in women: hirsutism, acne, female pattern hair loss — limited by liver toxicity (bicalutamide is now preferred)

## Dose & formulations
- Women (off-label): 62.5–250 mg/day with contraception

## Adverse effects
- Hepatotoxicity — may be fatal (boxed warning); dose-related
- Dry skin, GI upset, green-brown urine, photosensitivity

## Contraindications
- Liver disease; pregnancy

## Drug interactions
- Warfarin (INR rises)

## Monitoring
- LFT monthly for 4 months, then periodically

## Pregnancy & lactation
Contraindicated (feminisation of male fetus).

## Viva points
- Pure anti-androgen; fatal hepatotoxicity limits use in women

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.34; Khopkar (Antiandrogens). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
